title: Finite Hom equation descent through the fixed monoidal squares
statement:
theorem finiteHomSiteEquationDescent
    (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (_hl : l ≠ D.p)
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E]
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.Over (Spec (.of D.k))]
    [IsSeparated (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    (hdescent : ∀ n : ℕ, CoefFiniteHomDescent l E X n)
    (hsquare : ∀ (n m : ℕ) (h : m ≤ n), CoefFiniteHomSquare l E X h)
    (hmonoidal : ∀ (n m : ℕ) (h : m ≤ n),
      CoefFiniteHomMonoidalSquare
            (finiteHomEtaleClosed l E X n) (finiteHomEtaleClosed l E X m)
            (finiteIntrinsicClosed l E X n) (finiteIntrinsicClosed l E X m)
            (finiteHomEtaleReduction l E X h) (coefficientFiniteQuotientDerived l E X h)
            (finiteHomNu l E X n) (finiteHomNu l E X m)
            (finiteHomEtaleTensor l E X h) (coefFiniteHomProTensor l E X h)
            (finiteHomNuTensor l E X n) (finiteHomNuTensor l E X m)
            (coefFiniteHomSiteIso l E X h))
    (hquotient : ∀ (n m : ℕ) (h : m ≤ n), CoefFiniteHomQuotientCoherence l E X h) :
    ∀ (n m : ℕ) (h : m ≤ n),
      (CoefFiniteHomLawsOn
            (finiteHomEtaleClosed l E X n) (finiteHomEtaleClosed l E X m)
            (finiteHomEtaleReduction l E X h) (finiteHomEtaleTensor l E X h)
            (finiteTorConstructibleEtale l E (n + 1) (Nat.succ_pos n) X) →
            CoefFiniteHomLawsOn
              (finiteIntrinsicClosed l E X n) (finiteIntrinsicClosed l E X m)
              (coefficientFiniteQuotientDerived l E X h) (coefFiniteHomProTensor l E X h)
              (finiteTorConstructible l E (n + 1) (Nat.succ_pos n) X)) ∧
          CoefFiniteHomSuccessive l E X h

proof.text: Identify left-closed and specified right-closed transposes using the signed symmetry. Apply monoidal-square Hom transport and the supplied site Hom isomorphisms to carry naturality, arbitrary transpose and composition equations on etale-origin objects.

Paste the coefficient squares for a quotient tower. The supplied quotient coherence cancels the site components; the assumed etale coefficient equation gives the intrinsic one. Identity restriction has the specified adjunction mate, giving the normalized unit equation.

Use the supplied constructible descent hypothesis to choose etale witnesses for each intrinsic object. Naturality conjugates all obtained equations by their witness isomorphisms, whose inverses cancel. Thus the equations hold independently of witnesses.
